title: Lifting a compactification to its base with separated finite-type middle scheme
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme (quasi-compact as a topological space, with quasi-compact intersection of any two quasi-compact opens). Let $a_X:X\to S$ and $a_Y:Y\to S$ be schemes over $S$, and let $f:X\to Y$ satisfy $a_Y\circ f=a_X$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Assume $a_Y$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let
$$
c=(X\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{p}Y)
$$
be any compactification of the underlying scheme morphism $f$ [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], so $p\circ i=f$, $i$ is a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ is proper.

There is a unique structure morphism $a_Z:Z\to S$ making both $i$ and $p$ morphisms over $S$; it is $a_Z=a_Y\circ p$. For this structure, $a_Z$ is separated and of finite type, and $Z$ is quasi-compact as a scheme. The factorization $p\circ i=f$ therefore holds in $\mathit{Sch}/S$, with the same underlying open immersion and proper morphism. No finite-type or separatedness assumption on $a_X$ is required, and no existence or choice of $c$ is asserted.
